findings.title: Dayjs object identity comparison makes zero-length override check dead code
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two freshly created Dayjs objects with `===`, which is always false. The intended check for an empty override never runs, so such overrides fall through to the later range checks with unexpected results. Compare with `.isSame(...)` or compare `valueOf()` instead.

findings.title: Override day comparison mixes server-local and UTC formatting
findings.body: The override start is shifted by a computed offset and formatted with `format("YYYY MM DD")` using dayjs's local zone (`dayjs(date.start)` is not `.utc()`), and this is compared against `slotStartTime.format(...)`, which is UTC. The result depends on the server's TZ environment, so on a non-UTC server a date override can match the wrong day or miss the slot entirely. The comparison should be done in a single explicit timezone on both sides.

findings.title: Working-hours end is computed from the slot start, so the end bound is never checked
findings.body: `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` rather than the slot end, so `end === start`. The check `end > workingHour.endTime` therefore only tests the start time, and a slot starting inside working hours but running past the end is accepted. Also, the working-hour minutes are in organizer timezone while `slotStartTime` is UTC, so the comparison is inconsistent for non-UTC organizers.

findings.title: Working-hours check newly applied to all availability checks using UTC day and mismatched timezone
findings.body: checkIfIsAvailable now rejects slots outside `workingHours` for every caller, including fixed hosts whose `workingHours` were previously ignored at this point. `slotStartTime.day()` uses UTC weekday and UTC minutes, while `workingHour.startTime/endTime` are minutes in the organizer timezone. For organizers far from UTC, valid slots near midnight will be wrongly rejected or accepted. This is a behavior change beyond the described fix and is not covered by tests.

findings.title: Override timezone may be undefined and `Date.toString()` round-trip is lossy
findings.body: `override.timeZone` is optional in `TimeRange`, and `tz(undefined)` silently falls back to the local timezone, which yields a wrong offset. Additionally `override.start.toString()` drops milliseconds and relies on Date string parsing. Use `dayjs(override.start)` directly and handle a missing timezone explicitly (for example, fall back to the organizer timezone).

findings.title: Shifted override minutes ignore day rollover
findings.body: The startTime/endTime are computed as `hour()*60 + minute()` after shifting by the timezone offset, which discards the date. If the shifted time crosses midnight (for example, an override at 23:00 organizer time shifted to the next day for the invitee), the minute-of-day wraps to the wrong value, and the override window is placed at the wrong time of day. The override end is similarly affected. Offsets should be applied to the day-based timestamp, not the wrapped clock time.

findings.title: No test covers the round-robin fixed-host date override fix
findings.body: The PR's main claim is that date overrides of fixed hosts now restrict round-robin slots, but the only test added covers the invitee timezone change for a personal event. No test creates a round-robin event with a fixed host having a date override and checks that slots outside the override are removed. The new checkIfIsAvailable override and working-hours logic is therefore untested for the reported bug.
